name: EZIO2X4
description: A plug-in 2-relay, 4-input controller. Its relays switch small AC or DC loads on Insteon or X10 commands, and its inputs, two opto-isolated and two that can also measure voltages, send Insteon group commands when they change.

verification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) assigns 0x07/0x03 to the Compacta EZIO2X4 #5010D; the EZIOxx Advanced Details give 0x07/0x02 for EZIO as a whole. The catalog uses 0x07/0x03, the model's own entry.
The EZIOxx Advanced Details cover the whole EZIOxx line, from inputs-only to outputs-only models, and warn that a model may not support every command.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller links input N by tapping the SET button N times; that input N sends group N is read from that. The EZIOxx Advanced Details let each input's group number be changed.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller links input N by tapping the SET button N times; that input N sends group N is read from that. The EZIOxx Advanced Details let each input's group number be changed.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller links input N, as a controller or to be triggered as a responder, by tapping the SET button N times; that input N is group N is read from that. The EZIOxx Advanced Details let each input's group number be changed.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller links input N, as a controller or to be triggered as a responder, by tapping the SET button N times; that input N is group N is read from that. The EZIOxx Advanced Details let each input's group number be changed.

steps.text: Choose a power outlet close to the loads and sensors to be connected, away from moisture. Outdoors, use an approved weatherproof enclosure.
Connect each load between its relay's terminals: load 1 between R1_A and R1_B, and load 2 between R2_A and R2_B.
Connect the sensors or signals to the input terminals.
Plug the EZIO2X4 into an AC outlet.
steps.expect: LED may flash rapidly a few times, turns on and off for about 1 second, then glows steadily

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 10 to 12 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for input 1, twice for input 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes about once a second

steps.text: On the device to be controlled, press and hold its SET button for 3 to 4 seconds, or use that device's own method.
steps.expect: The device's LED flashes; the EZIO2X4's LED flashes, then keeps blinking about once a second

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds to end the linking session.

notes: This links an input as a controller. Repeat the step on the device to be controlled for each further device before ending the session.

X10: relays 1 and 2 answer X10 units 1 and 2, and the device takes all 16 units of its house code. To enable X10, press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds (the LED blinks slowly) and send an On from an X10 controller; the LED stops blinking. An Off disables it. The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller sends one On; the EZIOxx Advanced Details choose the house code on the X10 controller first and send 3 On commands in succession. This note follows the Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller.

steps.text: Put the controller in linking mode by holding the button that will control the EZIO2X4 until it shows linking mode, 4 to 10 seconds depending on the controller.
steps.expect: Controller LED blinks or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off; the controller's LED or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for relay 1 or twice for relay 2.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns on solidly

notes: To link a snapshot of both relays as they are, for the controller to recall, skip the taps: the Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller gives this first, and linking one relay as the other way.

steps.text: Put the controller in linking mode by holding the button that will control the EZIO2X4 until it shows linking mode, 4 to 10 seconds depending on the controller.
steps.expect: Controller LED blinks or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off; the controller's LED or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for input 1, twice for input 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 10 to 12 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns on solidly

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off

steps.text: Tap the SET button once, for relay 1.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns on solidly

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
steps.expect: The device acknowledges the Ping

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, for relay 1, and the device's group 1, input 1, to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the input's reports. Link inputs 2 to 4 the same way, with cmd2 0x02 to 0x04.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. The EZIOxx Advanced Details give Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with the group number in cmd2, but don't say whether it links an input as a controller.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 10 to 12 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for input 1, twice for input 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 18 to 20 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes about once a second

steps.text: On the device to be unlinked, press and hold its SET button for 3 to 4 seconds, or use that device's own method.
steps.expect: The device's LED flashes; the EZIO2X4's LED turns on solidly

notes: This stops a responder from being controlled by an input.

steps.text: Put the controller in unlinking mode, as its own instructions say.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes briefly, then turns on solidly; the controller's LED turns on solidly

steps.text: Unplug the EZIO2X4.
Wait about 10 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging it back in.
Keep holding the SET button for about 10 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: Unit goes through its normal power-on sequence

notes: The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller names the EZIO8T in this step.
Restores all settings to their factory values.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Repeat the last two steps for each other input linked to the Hub, groups 2 to 4, with cmd2 set to the group (0x02 to 0x04).
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes briefly, then turns on solidly

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps for the relays and the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode and Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub. The EZIOxx Advanced Details give Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with the group number in cmd2.

notes: Each relay is a switch rated 0.5 A at 30 V DC or 120 V AC, between terminals Rx_A and Rx_B. Timers can pulse a relay from 1 second to 255 minutes.

Inputs I1 and I2 are opto-isolated and need 3 to 30 V DC between their + and - terminals; for a dry contact, wire + to the +5 V terminal and the contact between - and GND. I3 and I4 are digital by default, on at 0 to 1 V DC and off at 3 to 5 V DC, and need a voltage, not a dry contact (a pull-up resistor to +5 V will do); software can set them to measure 0 to 5 V DC as a count from 0 to 1023 and alarm at set levels. The +5 V terminal supplies at most 20 mA.
Its ALL-Link database holds up to 30 links.

As a responder, a record whose Data 2 is 0x01 triggers the input in Data 3 (0x00 for input 1) as if it had turned on, so the input sends its own group command. Groups 1 and 2 are also relays 1 and 2, whose responder records the catalog gives for those groups; inputs 1 and 2 can be triggered the same way, with Data 3 0x00 or 0x01.

The Quick-Start Guide EZIO2X4—Model #5010D—2-Relay/4-Input Controller applies to firmware 2.2 and above. Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) records that 0x07/0x03 was first assigned to an EZIO3R I/O Module.
The Product Guide EZEye Ambient Light Sensor —Model #1011A notes that the EZIO2X4 can't supply the 8 V DC an EZEye needs.
